notes: Fixtures are generated by evals/generate_sessions.py (stdlib-only; content deterministic, timestamps relative to now). Run it immediately before every eval run — the skill narrows candidates to the last 7 days by file mtime and record timestamps, so stale fixtures silently empty the candidate list. If fixtures are copied into a run directory, mtimes must be preserved (cp -p / rsync -t). Both evals are dry runs: the prompt forbids real gh/GitHub calls and supplies the reporter login and feedback repo, so no network access or auth is needed and nothing is posted anywhere. The target skill in the fixtures is 'deploy-helper'; the fixture cast (sessions A–E) is documented at the top of generate_sessions.py.

evals.name: candidate-triage-and-issue-preview
evals.prompt: I want to file feedback issues for my recent deploy-helper skill sessions. My Claude Code session store is at evals/files/projects — use that directory instead of ~/.claude/projects. This is a dry run: do NOT run gh or contact GitHub in any way. Assume my GitHub login is testuser, the feedback repo is example-org/agent-feedback, and no feedback issues exist there yet. Show me the candidate sessions from the last 7 days, and for the one session that actually invoked deploy-helper, write the exact issue body you would post to issue-preview.md. Don't stop to ask me which session to pick.
evals.expected_output: A candidate list that classifies session A as a confirmed invocation, B as mentioned-only, C as skill maintenance, and omits D entirely; plus issue-preview.md containing a machine-parseable metadata comment, accurate session stats, and a synthesized per-turn transcript.
evals.ground_truth: Store contains 4 sessions. A (…0001, 2 days old): structured Skill invocation of deploy-helper; 2 real user prompts (1 follow-up) — the first is 'Deploy the latest build of the webapp to staging…'; tools Skill x1, Bash x3 (plus 1 sidechain-only exchange and 1 isMeta '<command-message>' record to be filtered); exactly 1 failed tool call (health-check timeout); model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001; CLI version 2.0.14 from session records. B (…0002): mentions/reads deploy-helper but never invokes it. C (…0003): edits /Users/dev/skills-sandbox/deploy-helper/SKILL.md — maintenance. D (…0004): unrelated, no mention of deploy-helper.
assertions: Identifies session …0001 as the (only) session with a confirmed deploy-helper invocation and uses it for the issue preview
Presents session …0002 as mentioned-but-not-confirmed-invoked (or an equivalent lower-confidence label), distinct from confirmed usage
Presents session …0003 as skill maintenance (editing deploy-helper's own files), not as regular usage
Does not list session …0004 as a candidate
The goal / first-prompt shown for session …0001 is the real typed prompt ('Deploy the latest build…'), not the isMeta '<command-message>' record or sidechain content
issue-preview.md contains an HTML comment metadata block including at least session_id, target_name, user_login, and submitted_at (the duplicate-detection payload)
issue-preview.md reports exactly 1 tool failure, 1 user follow-up, model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, and CLI version 2.0.14 sourced from the session records

The transcript in issue-preview.md is synthesized per turn (verbatim user prompt quotes plus a summarized description of agent activity and tools used), not a dump of raw JSONL records or tool arguments

The Suggestions section derives at least one suggestion from the user's follow-up prompt (the log-tailing follow-up implies deploy-helper should check logs after deploying), not only from the tool failure
No real gh/GitHub commands are executed (the dry-run constraint is respected)

evals.name: no-recent-sessions-stops
evals.prompt: Review my recent deploy-helper skill sessions and prepare feedback issues. My Claude Code session store is at evals/files/projects-stale — use that directory instead of ~/.claude/projects. Dry run: do NOT run gh or contact GitHub; assume my GitHub login is testuser and the feedback repo is example-org/agent-feedback.
evals.expected_output: Reports that there are no deploy-helper sessions inside the 7-day window and stops (or asks before widening); files no feedback for the ~30-day-old session on its own initiative.
evals.ground_truth: The store's only session (…0005) is a confirmed deploy-helper invocation, but it is ~30 days old — outside the 7-day lookback window (both its record timestamps and its file mtime are ~30 days in the past).
assertions: Reports that no deploy-helper sessions fall inside the 7-day lookback window
Does not silently widen the lookback window: it either stops after reporting, or explicitly asks for consent before considering older sessions
Does not present the ~30-day-old session …0005 as a recent candidate or prepare a feedback issue for it uninvited (acknowledging that an older session exists outside the window is fine)
Does not fabricate candidate sessions that are not in the store

evals.name: duplicate-guard-skips-submitted
evals.prompt:
I want to file feedback issues for my recent deploy-helper skill sessions. My Claude Code session store is at evals/files/projects — use that directory instead of ~/.claude/projects. This is a dry run: do NOT run gh or contact GitHub in any way. Assume my GitHub login is testuser and the feedback repo is example-org/agent-feedback. Instead of querying GitHub for existing issues, treat the following as the complete result of the existing-issues query (gh issue list --json number,title,url,state,body):

[{"number": 42, "title": "[deploy-helper feedback] 2026-08-05 — 3f2a1b04 — Deploy the latest build", "url": "https://github.com/example-org/agent-feedback/issues/42", "state": "OPEN", "body": "<!-- tool-feedback:metadata
session_id: 3f2a1b04-9c1d-4e6a-8b2f-000000000001
target_name: deploy-helper
user_login: testuser
-->
**TL;DR:** already filed"}]

Show me the candidate sessions, and prepare issue bodies (written to issue-preview.md files, not posted) only for confirmed-invocation sessions that have NOT already been submitted. Don't stop to ask me which sessions to pick.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes from the supplied existing-issues list that the only confirmed-invocation session (…0001) already has issue #42, marks it as already submitted, and prepares no new issue body for it or any other session.
evals.ground_truth: Same 4-session store as eval 0. Session A (…0001) is the only confirmed invocation, and the supplied existing-issue list contains a metadata block citing its session_id (issue #42). B is mention-only, C is maintenance, D unrelated — none qualifies for an issue. Correct behavior: candidate list with A marked already-submitted (linking issue #42), and no issue-preview files written.
assertions: Marks session …0001 as already submitted, citing the existing issue #42 (or its URL) from the supplied list
Does not prepare a new issue body for session …0001 (no issue-preview file and no metadata block for it in the report)
Does not prepare issue bodies for the mention-only (…0002), maintenance (…0003), or unrelated (…0004) sessions
No real gh/GitHub commands are executed (the dry-run constraint is respected)
